source_excerpt:
===INSTRUCTIONS TO GET RID OF THIS BLOATWARE===
You are removing a program that was installed on your PC without a real way out. You are turning Windows Security back on. You are not installing anything. You are not turning Defender off. If a command below is not about AnyTech365 / Panda / IntelliGuard / AntiScam, do not run it.
Hang up. Do not let anyone remote in “to help you uninstall.” If they are on the PC right now, unplug the network cable or turn Wi-Fi off.
Settings, Apps. Write down anything named Anytech365, IntelliGuard, Anti Scam, SysCleaner. Also look for TeamViewer, AnyDesk, Splashtop. If you see those remote tools, uninstall those first. That is just Settings, Uninstall.
Win+R, type appwiz.cpl , Enter. Uninstall SysCleaner, then IntelliGuard, then Anti Scam, then Anytech365 Security last. If Windows actually removes them, skip to step 8 (turn Defender back on). If Uninstall errors out, that is the trap. Keep going. You did not break it.
You may need Safe Mode only because their leftover files are locked. Start, Power, hold Shift, Restart. Troubleshoot, Advanced, Startup Settings, Restart, press 4 (Safe Mode). Try Uninstall in Apps again. If you see “Windows Installer cannot be started in safe mode,” leave it. That is a Windows Safe Mode limit, not you.
You need a real admin PowerShell window. On Windows 11 the word powershell in Run can flash and die. That is a stub. Task Manager (Ctrl+Shift+Esc), File, Run new task, paste only this, which is Microsoft’s PowerShell:
Check the admin box if it is there. Blue window that stays open is correct.
Their leftover Panda/Anytech services are set to start every boot. We are not disabling Windows. We are telling only those leftovers not to start. In the blue window:
Then these, one at a time. Quiet is success. These names are theirs, not Microsoft’s:
sp is s then p. If you type ps you get a different command.
To see if any of theirs are still set to auto-start, still in that same folder:
If one of those leftover names shows Start : 2, it will come back on reboot. Same pattern: sp TheName Start 4 (quotes if the name has a space). You want Start : 4 only on those Anytech/Panda names.
Restart the PC the normal way. Start, Power, Restart. No Shift. If the Anytech tray icon is gone and the laptop feels fast again, those leftovers did not start. Good.
Try Apps uninstall one more time. If their uninstaller still errors, do not turn their program back on to make the uninstaller happy. That is the catch-22. Leave it and delete the leftover folders.
Delete AnyTech365 AntiScam and IntelliGuard Bridge if they are still there. That is their install folder, not Windows.
AnyTech365 Security may refuse and say you need permission from SYSTEM. Do not click Continue on a hundred files. Boot Safe Mode again (step 3). Admin Command Prompt. These three only remove that leftover folder:
This is the point of the whole thing. Open Windows Security and turn your protections back on:
Virus and threat protection (real-time)
Update the virus definitions. Run a Quick scan. If Defender wants to quarantine Anytech leftovers, let it.
If the Virus and threat switch will not move, Defender may already be running. In admin cmd:
If it says RUNNING, you are fine. Try the switch again after a reboot.
A dead name in Apps with no icon and “cannot find the file” is a leftover list entry. It is not the program. You can ignore it.
Make sure they did not add a login. Admin cmd:
Your family’s account should be there. DefaultAccount, Guest, WDAGUtilityAccount are Windows. A name you do not know in Administrators is the one to worry about.
You should not need any of this. Uninstall should be one click. They built it so it is not. You are putting Windows back in charge of a PC they treated like a rental.
